strategy.thesis: Corporate accelerator run by The Walt Disney Company that pairs venture-backed, growth-stage entertainment and technology startups with Disney executives, mentorship, and bespoke strategic investment.

application_cycles: Annual; 2025 program ran July to November Demo Day
program.eligibility: Venture-backed, growth-stage startups in entertainment and technology aligned with Disney's business priorities (XR/immersive media, AI/ML, sports tech, robotics, connected play, haptics, Gen Alpha experiences).

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the Disney Accelerator site; companies also identified through Disney outreach and investor referrals (info@disneyaccelerator.com).

summary.en: The Disney Accelerator is The Walt Disney Company's corporate accelerator, launched in 2014 (initially with Techstars). It runs an intensive ~three-month program in Glendale, CA for ~5-10 venture-backed, growth-stage entertainment and tech startups, providing executive mentorship and bespoke investment capital.

aka: Comcast NBCUniversal LIFT Labs Accelerator powered by Techstars

strategy.thesis: Corporate accelerator run by Comcast NBCUniversal (with Sky) focused on media, AI, and connectivity startups, designed to accelerate commercial relationships and pilots with Comcast businesses.

program.eligibility: Startups in media, AI, and connectivity; the current Enterprise Accelerator targets pre-seed to Series B enterprise startups.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the LIFT Labs accelerator site.

summary.en: Comcast NBCUniversal LIFT Labs is Comcast's corporate accelerator, announced in 2017 and run from the Comcast Technology Center in Philadelphia. The original Techstars-powered program gave $120,000 for ~6% equity over 13 weeks; the current Enterprise Accelerator is an equity-free program for media/AI/connectivity startups designed to drive pilots with Comcast, NBCUniversal, and Sky.

verification_notes: Original program was Techstars-powered ($120K for 6% equity, 13 weeks). Current 'Enterprise Accelerator' is described as equity-free (5-6 weeks per some secondary sources), so terms have evolved; investment is no longer guaranteed. 43+ companies invested since 2018 inaugural cohort.

aka: Google for Startups Accelerator: North America

strategy.thesis: Equity-free corporate accelerator run by Google that gives high-potential, deeply technical startups mentorship from Google teams, product credits, and access to Google's AI/Cloud technologies.

application_cycles: Themed cohorts; e.g. applications open May 4, 2026, close June 30, 2026
program.eligibility: Startups demonstrating traction, ideally between Pre-seed and Series A, deeply technical and leveraging ML/AI.

application.how_to_apply: Apply online for the relevant themed North America cohort.

summary.en: Google for Startups Accelerator is Google's equity-free corporate accelerator. Its North America program is a 10-week, hybrid program for cohorts of 10-15 deeply technical, Pre-seed to Series A startups, offering Google mentorship, product/Cloud credits, and early access to Google AI products.

sources.title: Google for Startups Accelerator: North America
sources.supports: program length, cohort size, equity-free, eligibility, application dates
sources.quote: The Google for Startups Accelerator: North America is equity-free for all participating startups ... Each cohort of 10-15 startups comes together ... Ten weeks ... Startups demonstrating traction, ideally between Pre-seed and Series A stage

verification_notes: Equity-free; no cash investment, value is in mentorship and product/Cloud credits. Cohorts are themed (AI-first, Cloud AI, energy/grid, etc.), so number of batches per year and total portfolio count vary and were not verified to a single figure.

strategy.thesis: Mastercard's equity-free corporate startup engagement program connecting later-stage fintech startups with Mastercard's network, innovation labs, and co-innovation opportunities to scale commerce and payments solutions globally.

investment.raw: no upfront equity; potential investment support

program.eligibility: Later-stage fintech startups (typically Seed or Series A+) with proven solutions and real customers, across tracks: Acceptance, Emerging fintech, Blockchain & digital assets, Security, Small business, Open finance.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the Mastercard Start Path website to the relevant fintech track.

summary.en: Mastercard Start Path, founded in 2014, is Mastercard's equity-free, four-month virtual corporate startup engagement program. It has supported 350+ fintech startups, evaluating 1,500+ applications a year and selecting ~40, giving them access to Mastercard's global network, labs, and potential investment support.

sources.title: Mastercard Start Path Emerging Fintech Program 2025
sources.supports: founding year, startups supported, four-month virtual, equity-free, applications/selection
sources.quote: Since 2014, Mastercard has helped more than 350 startups grow ... a four-month, fully virtual accelerator ... evaluates more than 1,500 applications each year and selects approximately 40 startups ... The program takes no equity upfront

verification_notes: Mastercard official Start Path page returned HTTP 403; figures (350+ startups, 1,500 applications, ~40 selected, four-month, equity-free, founded 2014) corroborated by secondary source and CB Insights. Mastercard HQ is Purchase, NY.

strategy.thesis: Corporate health-tech accelerator run by Cedars-Sinai (originally with Techstars) that gives startups capital, clinical and market expertise, and access to 300+ Cedars-Sinai clinicians and executives to validate and commercialize healthcare innovations.

program.location: Cedars-Sinai Innovation Space, West Hollywood / Los Angeles, CA
application_cycles: Annual cohorts; Accelerator+ is now a 12-month venture-building program
program.eligibility: Health-tech startups; the Accelerator+ model targets Seed+ and Late Seed healthcare companies advancing toward commercialization.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the Cedars-Sinai Accelerator website.

summary.en: The Cedars-Sinai Accelerator is the Cedars-Sinai health system's corporate accelerator, launched in 2016 with Techstars. The original 13-week program gave $100,000 for ~6% equity and access to 300+ clinicians; it has evolved into Accelerator+, a 12-month venture-building platform for Seed+/Late Seed healthcare startups. It has run 10 classes covering 91 companies.

Techstars later ran a consortium healthcare program with Cedars-Sinai, Point32Health, UCI Health, and UnitedHealthcare.

strategy.thesis: Wells Fargo's corporate accelerator that advances startups building solutions for enterprise customers inside and outside financial services, aligning them with Wells Fargo business and technology leaders via a non-exclusive, minority-equity program.

application_cycles: Historically rolling; not currently accepting applications
program.eligibility: Seed to early-stage startups (software, IT, AI) building solutions for enterprise / financial services customers.

application.how_to_apply: Historically applied via the Wells Fargo accelerator site; program not currently accepting applications.

summary.en: The Wells Fargo Startup Accelerator is Wells Fargo's corporate accelerator (launched 2014): a virtual, six-month, non-exclusive program for seed/early-stage startups building enterprise and financial-services solutions, offering up to $1 million in funding for a minority equity stake. It is not currently accepting applications.

sources.title: Wells Fargo Startup Accelerator
sources.supports: program description, six-month virtual non-exclusive
sources.quote: The virtual, six-month, non-exclusive program aligns companies with Wells Fargo business and technology leaders to help refine the launch of their ideas.

sources.supports: funding amount, minority equity, not accepting applications
sources.quote: offers $50K to $500K in funding with a minority equity stake ... startups are eligible to receive up to $1 million in funding

verification_notes: Six-month virtual program with up to $1M funding for a minority equity stake confirmed via official site + secondary source; exact check range and current status uncertain. Secondary sources indicate it is not currently accepting applications, hence status set to dormant. Wells Fargo also runs a separate cleantech program (Innovation Incubator / IN2, see separate entry).

strategy.thesis: Non-dilutive cleantech incubator funded by the Wells Fargo Foundation and co-administered with the U.S. National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), supporting early-stage cleantech/agtech startups with technical validation and grants.

investment.raw: up to $250,000 non-dilutive technical assistance per company

program.location: NREL, Golden, Colorado + channel partner network
application_cycles: Nominated by 60+ channel partners, then reviewed
program.eligibility: Early-stage cleantech/agtech startups working on energy, transportation, food systems, energy storage, water, and smart communities; nominated by IN² channel partners.

application.how_to_apply: Companies are nominated by IN²'s nationwide network of channel partners, then reviewed by Wells Fargo, NREL, and the IN² advisory board.

summary.en: The Wells Fargo Innovation Incubator (IN²) is a $50M non-dilutive cleantech incubator funded by the Wells Fargo Foundation and co-administered with NREL. Launched in 2014, it gives early-stage cleantech/agtech startups up to $250,000 each in non-dilutive technical assistance; over 10 years it supported 12 cohorts.

sources.title: Wells Fargo Innovation Incubator (IN2)
sources.supports: $50M program, non-dilutive, $250k per company, NREL co-administration
sources.quote: IN2 is a $50 million clean-technology incubator and platform funded by the Wells Fargo Foundation ... receive up to $250,000 in technical assistance from the laboratory

sources.title: IN² at 10 Years
sources.supports: founding 2014, 12 cohorts, follow-on funding ratio
sources.quote: Over the past 10 years, IN2 has supported 12 cohorts of startup companies with up to $250,000 each in nondilutive funding.

verification_notes: Non-dilutive (no equity). Co-administered with NREL (a federal lab), so it straddles corporate-accelerator and government-program; included here as a Wells Fargo Foundation-funded corporate open-innovation program. Channel-partner nomination model rather than open application.

strategy.thesis: Equity-free corporate accelerator run by T-Mobile that helps startups develop and commercialize products leveraging T-Mobile's nationwide 5G network, with proofs-of-concept, mentorship, and corporate visibility.

program.location: Bellevue, WA and Overland Park, KS
program.eligibility: Companies of any stage, including growth-stage startups and scaling companies, building products/services leveraging T-Mobile's 5G network aligned with corporate strategic goals.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the T-Mobile Accelerator site; reviewed by a selection committee with follow-up interviews.

summary.en: The T-Mobile Accelerator is T-Mobile's equity-free corporate accelerator based in Bellevue, WA (and Overland Park, KS). Its hybrid, ~three-month themed cohorts help startups of any stage build and commercialize products on T-Mobile's 5G network. It has worked with 75 startups that have raised over $96M, with 80% still in business.

strategy.thesis: Equity-free, no-fee corporate accelerator launched by Intel for early-stage deep tech startups, providing expert-led workshops, mentorship, and access to Intel's network and ecosystem.

program.location: Boston, MA (US program); also Israel, Europe, UK
program.eligibility: Early-stage (ideation, pre-seed, seed) deep tech startups.

application.how_to_apply: Apply via the Intel Ignite website for the relevant regional cohort.

summary.en: Intel Ignite is Intel's equity-free, no-fee corporate accelerator for early-stage deep tech startups, launched in 2019. It runs 12-week cohorts of ~10 startups twice a year, including a US program based in Boston, plus programs in Israel, Europe, and the UK.

sources.supports: founded 2019, 12 weeks, ~10 startups, equity-free, no fees, twice a year, locations
sources.quote: launched in 2019 by Intel ... Intel Ignite takes no equity stake in the companies it champions and charges no program fees. Twice a year, in the spring and fall, Intel Ignite brings together cohorts of ten startups in its Israeli, European, US, and UK offices for 12 weeks

verification_notes: Equity-free and no fees. Note: Intel briefly shut Ignite down in 2024 amid Intel restructuring, and an independent spin-off ('Ignite') relaunched offering innovation services; however intelignite.com still operates as Intel's program and ran a Spring 2024 US Boston cohort. Status set to active with this caveat.

strategy.thesis: Global innovation platform that runs equity-free, corporate-sponsored vertical accelerator programs connecting startups with hundreds of corporate partners across industries, and also invests directly in some startups.

program.eligibility: Startups across many verticals (fintech, mobility, agtech, retail, energy, insurtech, IoT, real estate, travel, health, etc.) sponsored by corporate partners.

application.how_to_apply: Apply to a relevant vertical accelerator program via the Plug and Play site.

summary.en: Plug and Play Tech Center, founded in 2006 in Sunnyvale, CA, is a global open-innovation platform that runs equity-free, corporate-sponsored vertical accelerator programs connecting startups with hundreds of corporate partners, while also making direct investments. Wikipedia describes it as the most active startup accelerator in the world (~929 deals/year); past alumni include PayPal, Dropbox, and LendingClub.

sources.quote: Founded 2006 ... headquartered in Sunnyvale, California ... the most active startup accelerator in the world with an average deal count of 929 per year ... US$500 million (2023) ... Notable companies that Plug and Play invested in include PayPal, LendingClub and Dropbox

verification_notes: Plug and Play is an open-innovation platform that runs corporate-sponsored accelerator programs (equity-free for the accelerator) AND makes direct VC investments — so it straddles accelerator and VC. Included here for its corporate-sponsored accelerator model. Program length/cohort details vary by vertical and were not pinned to a single figure. AUM and deal-count figures from Wikipedia (2023).
